test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Advanced Full Test - 01
subject: general
question: If the net factor income earned from the rest of the world is zero, which one of the following relationships must necessarily be true in national income accounting?

options.text: Gross National Product is equal to Net National Product
Gross Domestic Product is equal to Gross National Product
Gross Domestic Product is greater than Gross National Product
Gross Domestic Product is equal to National Income.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option B**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **national income accounting**, the relationship between **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** and **Gross National Product (GNP)** depends on **Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)**, which represents the difference between income earned by residents from abroad and income earned by foreigners domestically. When **NFIA is zero**, domestic and national product values coincide.
 
• **GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)**. If **NFIA = 0**, then **GNP = GDP**. Hence, **Option B is correct**.
 
• **Gross National Product** and **Net National Product** differ due to **depreciation**; even if NFIA is zero, depreciation still exists. Hence, **Option A is incorrect**.
 
• If NFIA is zero, **GDP cannot be greater than GNP**; both are equal. Hence, **Option C is incorrect**.
 
• **National Income** is obtained after subtracting **depreciation** and **net indirect taxes** from GDP or GNP; therefore, GDP cannot be equal to National Income merely because NFIA is zero. Hence, **Option D is incorrect**.

**Thus, Gross Domestic Product is equal to Gross National Product → Option B. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GDP** measures income generated **within domestic territory**.
 
• **GNP** measures income generated by **nationals**, irrespective of location.
 
• **NFIA** can be positive (remittances-dominated economies) or negative (foreign-investment-heavy economies).
 
• **National Income = NNP at factor cost**, not GDP or GNP.
